sections.heading: Glossary term: Asteroid
sections.body: An asteroid is a small body that orbits around the Sun or another star or stellar remnant. Asteroids are solid bodies of various compositions: a number of them are rich in carbon, some contain more rocky material (silicates), and others are mainly composed of metals. Most asteroids are piles of rubble bound together by gravity, with bumpy, uneven shapes. Some asteroids have moons – other small asteroids which orbit them. Asteroids are smaller than dwarf planets (which have enough mass for gravity to pull them into a nearly round shape). They are larger than meteoroids; the lower size limit of an asteroid is commonly set at between one and 10 meters across. If heating by the Sun or star causes the small body to emit gas and dust, the body is a comet and not an asteroid (although the distinction is not always clear). Historically, the name asteroid was given to any astronomical body that orbits the Sun that was too small to resolve with a telescope. As  they appeared as star-like points through a telescope they were named asteroids after the Greek word for star-like.

sections.source_html:
Glossary term: Asteroid

Description: An asteroid is a small body that orbits around the Sun or another star or stellar remnant. Asteroids are solid bodies of various compositions: a number of them are rich in carbon, some contain more rocky material (silicates), and others are mainly composed of metals.

Most asteroids are piles of rubble bound together by gravity, with bumpy, uneven shapes. Some asteroids have moons – other small asteroids which orbit them.

Asteroids are smaller than dwarf planets (which have enough mass for gravity to pull them into a nearly round shape). They are larger than meteoroids; the lower size limit of an asteroid is commonly set at between one and 10 meters across. If heating by the Sun or star causes the small body to emit gas and dust, the body is a comet and not an asteroid (although the distinction is not always clear).

Historically, the name asteroid was given to any astronomical body that orbits the Sun that was too small to resolve with a telescope. As they appeared as star-like points through a telescope they were named asteroids after the Greek word for star-like.

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. You can find a full list of credits here. All glossary terms and their definitions are released under a Creative Commons CC BY-4.0 license and should be credited to "IAU OAE".

If you notice a factual error in this glossary definition then please get in touch.
sections.body_ru: Астероид — небольшое твёрдое тело, которое обращается вокруг Солнца, другой звезды или звёздного остатка. Одни астероиды богаты углеродом, другие состоят преимущественно из силикатных пород, третьи — главным образом из металлов. Многие астероиды имеют неправильную форму и состоят из обломков, удерживаемых вместе собственной гравитацией. У некоторых есть более мелкие спутники. Обычно астероиды меньше карликовых планет, массы которых достаточно, чтобы собственная гравитация придала им почти округлую форму. Астероиды крупнее метеороидов. Граница условна: в разных классификациях для нижнего предела размера астероида берут величины порядка 1–10 м. Для комет характерно выделение газа и пыли при нагреве звездой. Граница между классами бывает размытой, поскольку некоторые астероиды тоже проявляют кометную активность. Исторически так называли тела на орбитах вокруг Солнца, которые в телескоп выглядели как точки без различимого диска. Отсюда название «астероид», то есть «звездоподобный».

Ida and Dactyl

Caption: This picture of the asteroid Ida with its satellite Dactyl was taken by the Galileo space probe in August 1993 from a range of 10,870 kilometers (6,755 miles). Ida is a heavily cratered, irregularly shaped asteroid in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. This image is proof that asteroids like the 56 km large Ida can possess their own moons.

media.caption_en: This picture of the asteroid Ida with its satellite Dactyl was taken by the Galileo space probe in August 1993 from a range of 10,870 kilometers (6,755 miles). Ida is a heavily cratered, irregularly shaped asteroid in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. This image is proof that asteroids like the 56 km large Ida can possess their own moons.
media.caption_ru: Этот снимок астероида Ида с его спутником Дактилем был сделан космическим зондом «Галилео» в августе 1993 года с расстояния 10 870 километров (6 755 миль). Ида — сильно кратерированный астероид неправильной формы в главном поясе астероидов между Марсом и Юпитером. Это изображение является доказательством того, что такие астероиды, как Ида размером 56 км, могут иметь собственные луны.
